title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, at most one repair) improves the correctness of LLM-generated network configurations relative to single-shot initial generation. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and an automated network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes). The hosted model was gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed all verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 tasks (100%). The paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI [0.00, 0.015]); discordant pairs n10=1, n01=0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair invocation that corrected a multi‑step ordering failure. We report the preregistration, execution artifacts, complete paired analysis, a short failure-mode diagnosis, and limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into low-level device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational adoption requires that generated artifacts satisfy deterministic invariants such as reachability, policy compliance, loop‑freedom, and ordered-change/workflow constraints. Prior work has proposed intent→configuration pipelines and advocated pairing generation with external validators or repair loops to mitigate unsafe outputs [1], [2]. Surveys and safety discussions emphasize LLM failure modes and recommend guardrails and verification for operational use [3], [5]. However, end‑to‑end, verifier-backed empirical results quantifying guarded pipeline effects on operational invariants in NetOps are limited. This study asks: under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial generation reused for baseline and guarded episodes), to what extent does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (one permitted repair call) reduce invariant violations relative to the single-shot initial generation? Our confirmatory contribution is a preregistered paired evaluation (N=200 tasks) executed with a deterministic synthetic task generator, a deterministic network verifier, and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini), with all artifacts archived.
sections.related_work: Intent→configuration systems and prototype benchmarks have advanced rapidly; NetConfEval and related efforts study whether LLMs can assist configuration synthesis and highlight verification needs [1]. Formal/verifier-driven approaches to network configuration verification provide structured oracles for correctness evaluation and have motivated generator+validator designs in networking [2]. Cross-domain results show that generate→validate→repair patterns can improve verifiability (program repair, decompilation, code synthesis), but those demonstrations are primarily in software-engineering domains rather than NetOps-specific pipelines [4]. Reporting and evaluation guidelines emphasize preregistration and transparent artifact disclosure for LLM studies [3]. Our experiment positions a tightly controlled, verifier-centered empirical test within this landscape and supplies a full archived execution trace to support reproducibility and follow-up work.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 (confirmatory paired binary design) before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion of tasks with all-specified‑invariants passing the deterministic verifier). Sampling and tasks: 200 deterministic intent→configuration tasks generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; tasks targeted very_hard and extreme workflow patterns. Inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination checks, and the single shared_initial_candidate generation semantics were fixed in the preregistration. Execution and model: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter called the hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial generation per task was sampled and reused for both paired episodes); at most one repair call per task permitted. The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Validation and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executed a full intent-constraint validation including syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, encoded workflow/ordering policies, and network-level invariants; per-pair outcome is binary ('all invariants pass' vs 'any invariant fails'). Analysis plan: primary confirmatory test using an exact McNemar-style paired test with discordant-pair reporting; report per-condition pass rates with 95% Wilson CIs and paired bootstrap percentile CI for the risk difference (bootstrap resamples = 10,000; seed = 1729). Accounting clarification (archived provider_call_audit): the execution manifest records model_calls_used = 201 while completed_episode_count = 400 because shared_initial_candidate semantics produced exactly 200 shared initial-generation calls (one per pair) plus one repair-stage call invoked by the guarded pipeline (stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1), yielding total hosted_model_call_event_count = 201; each shared initial candidate was reused by both the baseline and guarded episodes per pair. All prompts, provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, and analysis outputs were archived and are referenced in the execution manifest.
sections.results: Execution: The run completed per preregistration (planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400). Provider/model accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1) consistent with shared_initial_candidate semantics and the single allowed repair call. Primary confirmatory outcome: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency table: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (columns: baseline; rows: guarded). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the difference = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair activity: the guarded pipeline invoked the single permitted repair once; that repair converted the lone baseline failure into a guarded success. Exploratory diagnostics: the repaired task's validator trace shows a multi-step maintenance ordering constraint spanning multiple interfaces (archived task and validator trace referenced in the execution manifest). There were no exclusions, no unscorable episodes, and no persistent unparsable outputs under the preregistered handling rules.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: Under the chosen synthetic corpus, verifier encoding of operational invariants, and gpt-5-mini generation, single-shot LLM outputs already satisfied verifier-specified invariants in 199/200 tasks; the guarded pipeline's single repair corrected one remaining multi-step ordering failure. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, the paired difference is attributable solely to verifier-triggered repair (the initial candidate was identical for baseline and guarded episodes). Statistical perspective: with only one discordant pair the observed effect is extremely small and the confirmatory test is non-significant (p = 1.0); the 95% paired-bootstrap CI includes zero and upper-bounds the observed absolute improvement at 1.5 percentage points. Practical and validity notes: the preregistration's power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate in the 45–65% range to detect a 10–15 percentage-point change; the observed baseline (~99.5%) was far higher, so the originally planned sensitivity was not realized and the study cannot rule out small practical differences under other task/model distributions. Threats to validity: internal validity is constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics (no independent first-pass comparisons), deterministic verifier correctness (oracle limitations), and a single-model evaluation. Construct validity: the verifier enforces encoded invariants but may not capture live-device runtime semantics. External validity: tasks are synthetic, topologies controlled, and only gpt-5-mini was tested; no adversarial/poisoning experiments were executed. Operational implication (bounded claim): deterministic verifier gates plus bounded repair can remediate specific multi-step ordering failures, but these results do not establish general production benefits without broader, multi-model, and live-device evaluation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-guarded intent→configuration pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. In this deterministic synthetic task corpus with gpt-5-mini, single-shot generation yielded very high verifier compliance (199/200), and a single verifier-triggered repair converted the sole failing case into success, producing a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points). The study documents the end-to-end generator→validator→repair pipeline and archives complete artifacts to support reproducibility. Future work should evaluate multiple models, larger and more diverse task banks including noisy or partial state and live-device semantics, independent first-pass comparisons when permitted by design, adversarial contamination, and richer runtime oracles. All experimental artifacts and the execution manifest are archived per the track policy.

limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and the deterministic verifier; they do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent prompt-engineering or constrained-generation effects.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
